questiontext.text: The Observer pattern defines what kind of dependency between objects?

feedback.text: Correct — one subject, many observers.
Observer supports many dependents, not just one.
That describes Layered architecture.
That describes Pipes and Filters.

generalfeedback.text: Observer establishes a one-to-many relationship so that when one subject changes, all dependents are updated.

questiontext.text: When the subject's state changes, what happens to its observers?

answer.text: All registered observers are notified automatically

feedback.text: Correct — notification is automatic.

answer.text: Observers must poll the subject on a timer

feedback.text: No — the subject pushes notifications; polling is not required.

answer.text: Only the first observer is notified

feedback.text: All registered observers are notified.
The subject notifies observers; it does not rebuild.

generalfeedback.text: The subject keeps a list of observers and calls their update method whenever its state changes.

questiontext.text: How do observers control whether they receive updates?

feedback.text: Correct — subscription is dynamic.

answer.text: They inherit from the subject class

feedback.text: Observer favors composition over inheritance here.

answer.text: They edit the subject's source code

feedback.text: No source edits are needed; they just subscribe.

answer.text: They cannot; the set is fixed at compile time

feedback.text: Observers can be added or removed at run time.

generalfeedback.text: Observers subscribe/unsubscribe at run time, giving loose coupling between the subject and its dependents.

questiontext.text: At the object level, the Observer pattern is also known as ______.

feedback.text: Correct — the subject publishes and observers subscribe.
MVC uses Observer but is a different, larger pattern.
Unrelated — DI is about supplying dependencies.
Unrelated pipeline pattern.

generalfeedback.text: At the object level Observer is the publish-subscribe idea: the subject publishes state changes; observers subscribe to receive them.

questiontext.text: Which statements about the Observer pattern are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: It promotes loose coupling between subject and observers

feedback.text: Yes — the subject only knows an observer interface.

answer.text: Observers can be added or removed at run time

feedback.text: Yes — subscription is dynamic.

answer.text: The subject must know each observer's concrete class

feedback.text: No — it only depends on an abstract observer interface.
No — Observer is behavioral.

generalfeedback.text: Observer is behavioral: a subject notifies a dynamic set of loosely coupled observers through an abstract interface.

questiontext.text: In the Observer pattern, changing the subject's state automatically notifies all subscribed observers.

feedback.text: Correct — that is the defining behavior.
Automatic notification is exactly what Observer provides.

questiontext.text: The Observer pattern tightly couples the subject to each observer's concrete implementation.

feedback.text: No — Observer aims for loose coupling via an interface.
Correct — it is loosely coupled through an observer interface.

questiontext.text: The behavioral pattern defining a one-to-many dependency where dependents are notified of state changes is the ______ pattern. (one word, English)

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Accepted — the subject is the notifying role.
